How to check LoloBuy QC photos before shipping.

A practical method for comparing warehouse evidence with the product you actually ordered.

⌕

Product research & QC · 10 minute read

LoloBuy QC photos checklist: what to inspect before parcel submission

LoloBuy QC photos are most useful when you compare them with a precise record of what you ordered. A quick glance can reveal an obvious color or model problem, but a reliable check is more systematic: confirm the specification text, examine every image, compare visible details with the seller listing, review the recorded weight and dimensions, and request a targeted extra photo when the standard views do not answer an important question.

The current LoloBuy warehouse and order-detail interfaces can display a quality inspection report with an inspector label, ordinary or HD photos, weight or net weight, and volume or net volume. Photos can be previewed and downloaded. These are useful records, but they are not a guarantee of authenticity, hidden materials, internal function or future delivery condition.

1. Build your reference sheet before the item arrives

Good QC begins at checkout. Save the product link, seller name, order number, selected specification, quantity and the seller images that describe the chosen option. For clothing, keep the seller’s measurement table. For electronics or accessories, record the exact model, connector, color and included components shown in the listing.

Write the selection as one unambiguous line: for example, product model, color, seller size and quantity. Do not rely on a thumbnail or translated title alone. A marketplace listing may combine several variants under the same page, and the main image may not represent the SKU you paid for.

Keep evidence private and organized by order number. A simple folder containing the confirmation screen, selected-SKU text and relevant listing images makes the warehouse report easier to judge. It also prevents a later disagreement from becoming a comparison between memory and a listing that may have changed.

2. Confirm the warehouse record belongs to the right item

Open the order detail or warehouse item and match its order number, product title, image and specification text with your reference sheet. Check the quantity as well. If you ordered two identical items, one photo may show both together or the records may be separated; use the item data shown in your account rather than assuming the photo arrangement.

Read the QC report fields before studying cosmetic details. LoloBuy’s current interface can show the quality inspector and recorded measurements. The warehouse page can also display the selected SKU properties. A mismatch in model, size label or color name is a higher-priority issue than a minor variation caused by lighting.

If the report clearly belongs to another product or the specification text conflicts with the order, stop before parcel submission. Preserve screenshots of the order selection and warehouse record, then ask support to identify the item. Shipping first removes the opportunity to clarify it while the goods are still in the warehouse.

3. Inspect every ordinary QC photo in a fixed order

Start with the complete shape of the item, then move from front to back and from wide views to close details. Confirm the visible color family, silhouette, major panels, closures, printed text, logos, hardware and included pieces. Compare the same area in the seller image and warehouse photo instead of comparing overall impressions.

For clothing, look at the front, back, collar, cuffs, hem, visible stitching, label and size tag when shown. Check whether the ordered set contains every stated piece. A photo cannot prove how a garment fits, and perspective can distort proportions, so use visible measurements or seller dimensions rather than guessing fit from the model image.

For shoes, check that both shoes form a pair, the stated size is visible when possible, the colorway matches, and the outsole, heel, toe box and obvious surface finish look consistent. For bags and accessories, inspect straps, handles, zippers, fasteners and visible attachments. For electronics, confirm the external model, plug or connector and included accessories, but do not infer internal condition from an exterior photo.

4. Separate a visible defect from a photographic effect

Warehouse lighting, camera white balance, compression and reflections can change how color and texture appear. A single shadow is not automatically a stain, and a highlight on glossy material is not necessarily a scratch. Compare the same area across multiple photos before reaching a conclusion.

Look for evidence that persists: a mark visible from more than one angle, an uneven seam that follows the construction, a missing component, a different label, or a shape that conflicts with the ordered model. When only one image raises concern, frame the issue as a question rather than a verdict.

Zoom in, but remember that enlarging a low-resolution image does not create new detail. Downloading the original available photo can make comparison easier. LoloBuy’s current QC report supports photo downloads and batch downloads, which is useful for keeping the complete evidence set together.

5. Read weight and dimensions as logistics evidence

The quality report can show gross or net weight and gross or net dimensions, depending on the data available for that item. These figures help identify unusually large packaging, compare similar items and prepare for later parcel decisions. They are not a product-performance test.

Check which label accompanies the number. Weight and net weight are not interchangeable, just as volume and net volume may describe different packing states. Do not compare an unpacked seller claim with a gross warehouse record as if they measure the same thing.

A difference does not automatically prove an error. Retail packaging, protective material, accessories and measurement methods can affect the record. If the figure seems impossible for the ordered item, ask which packing state was measured and request clarification before using it in a shipping estimate.

6. Request an HD photo only for a specific decision

LoloBuy’s current HD-photo form allows multiple photo requests. Each request includes a written remark and can include a reference image, subject to the limits displayed in the live form. The total is calculated from the current service configuration, so check the shown amount rather than relying on an old price.

A useful request tells the photographer exactly what must be visible: “Photograph the size tag straight on,” “Show the connector and printed model number,” or “Measure the insole from heel to toe beside a ruler.” Add a marked reference image when words alone could point to the wrong area.

Avoid vague instructions such as “check quality” or “take more pictures.” They do not define the evidence you need. One targeted image that resolves a purchase decision is more valuable than several general angles that repeat the ordinary QC set.

7. Know what QC photos cannot establish

Visual inspection can document visible condition at the time of photography. It cannot by itself authenticate a branded item, verify fiber composition, prove battery health, test waterproofing or guarantee that an electronic device performs correctly. Unless a specific test is offered and recorded in your transaction, do not assume it occurred.

QC also does not guarantee that an item will remain unchanged through repacking and international transport. Parcel packaging, route restrictions and carrier handling are later stages. Keep the warehouse QC decision separate from the parcel-preparation decision.

Finally, a normal photo does not erase seller-policy limits. If a concern matters, review the current order status and use the official support or after-sales route while the item remains identifiable. The product-detail guidance states that buyers can contact the shopping provider about returns or exchanges according to the applicable agreement and service rules; it does not promise the same outcome for every item.

8. Report a mismatch with a compact evidence set

Describe the issue in observable terms. Include the private order or item reference, ordered specification, QC photo number, exact area of concern and the seller-listing evidence used for comparison. A marked screenshot can show the location, but keep the unmarked original as well.

Use language such as “The order shows navy, while the warehouse specification shows black” or “The listed set includes two pieces, but only one is visible.” Avoid unsupported conclusions about intent or authenticity. Ask what can be verified and what options apply to that order.

Do not publish full order numbers, tracking data, names, addresses or account details in a public review. Support needs enough information to find the transaction, while public readers do not need your identifiers.

A final LoloBuy QC photos checklist

Before submitting a parcel, match the order number, title, SKU, color, size or model and quantity. Review every ordinary and HD photo. Check visible construction, included pieces, labels and major surfaces. Read the weight and dimensions with their correct gross or net labels. Request a targeted extra photo if one important question remains.

Then make one of three decisions: accept the item for parcel preparation, request more evidence, or contact support about a documented mismatch. Do not let a parcel deadline or excitement about shipping replace the comparison. The purpose of QC is not to declare an item perfect; it is to make the next decision using the best visible evidence currently available.
